subtitle: Shrimp in fiery red chile sauce
verso: Shrimp a la diabla: one bite and you can't say a word.
story: Shrimp in a hot, glossy sauce of guajillo, chile de árbol and chipotle, fried in butter. A la diabla means devil-style: as hot as you dare. White rice on the side puts out the fire.

ingredients.title: The shrimp
items: 1½ lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails on

ingredients.title: The diabla sauce
items: ½ cup water or shrimp broth

steps: Toast the guajillos and chiles de árbol a few seconds in a dry pan. Soak in hot water 10 minutes.
Blend the soaked chiles with the chipotles, tomatoes, onion, garlic, oregano and [[½ cup]] water until smooth. Strain.
Heat the butter and oil in a wide pan. Pour in the sauce and fry it 6–8 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and thickens. Season with salt.
Add the shrimp in one layer and cook 2–3 minutes per side, until pink and curled.
Serve right away with rice, lime and bolillo.
pressureNote: No pressure-cooker version. Shrimp need only a few minutes in the pan.
tips: Set the heat with the chiles de árbol: 4 is spicy, 8 is a la diabla.
Don't crowd the pan, and pull the shrimp as soon as they curl into a C. An O means overcooked.

variations.name: Camarones al Mojo de Ajo
variations.subtitle: Garlic butter shrimp
variations.note: The mild one at the seafood restaurant: shrimp in golden garlic, butter and lime.

items: 1 chile guajillo, cut in thin rings, optional

steps: Warm the oil and butter over low heat and cook the garlic and guajillo slowly, 5–6 minutes, until the garlic is golden. Don't let it burn.
Raise the heat, add the shrimp and cook 2–3 minutes per side.
Add the lime juice, salt and parsley, toss and serve with rice.
